Posterior credible intervals on a fitted mvgam model

Source: R/brms_wrappers.mvgam.R
posterior_interval.mvgam.Rd

Central quantile intervals of the posterior draws of parameters. The parameters are chosen as in as.matrix.mvgam().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
posterior_interval(object, pars = NULL, variable = NULL, prob = 0.95, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted mvgam object.

pars

Deprecated alias for variable.

variable

Either a keyword shortcut, a character vector of parameter names, or (when regex = TRUE) a vector of regular expressions. Recognised keywords:

  • "betas": population-level coefficients, the set brms::fixef() reports (b_*, bs_* and bsp_*).

  • "obs_params": observation-family distributional parameters (sigma, phi, shape, ...).

  • "smooth_params": smooth-term standard deviations (sds_*).

  • "trend_betas": the trend formula's population-level coefficients (b_*_trend, bs_*_trend and bsp_*_trend).

  • "trend_params": trend-dynamics parameters (autoregressive coefficients, innovation SDs, ...).

  • "trend_smooth_params": trend-side smooth SDs.

NULL (the default) returns every parameter. A bare vector name, such as "sigma_trend", selects every element. Group-level effects, factor loadings and latent states have no keyword. Select them by name. variables.mvgam() lists the names a fit holds.

prob

Numeric in (0, 1). The probability mass each interval holds. Defaults to 0.95.

...

Further arguments of as.matrix.mvgam(), such as regex.

Value

A numeric matrix with one row per parameter and two columns, the lower and upper bounds.

See also

predictive_interval.mvgam() gives intervals of predictive draws. summary.mvgam() reports intervals with convergence diagnostics.

Other posterior summaries: VarCorr.mvgam(), bibtex(), how_to_cite.mvgam(), hypothesis.mvgam(), index-mvgam, mcmc_plot.mvgam(), methods_md(), mvgam_draws, pairs.mvgam(), ranef.mvgam(), smooths.mvgam(), summary.mvgam()

Author

Nicholas J Clark

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(13)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                    n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x, k = 5), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
             data = simdat$data_train, family = poisson(),
             chains = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 5 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# 90 percent intervals of the autoregression and its innovation SD
posterior_interval(mod, variable = c("ar1_trend", "sigma_trend"),
                   prob = 0.9)
#>                              5%       95%
#> ar1_trend[series_1]   0.3155002 0.7866585
#> sigma_trend[series_1] 0.3593428 0.5964314

# Next: summary() reports these with convergence diagnostics
# }
